title: タイミングとアスペクト — 間に／うちに／ところだ／たばかり

grammarPoints.rule: あいだ (間) marks a stretch of time as a single continuous span — the WHOLE TIME something else was true, not one point inside it. せんせいが はなしている あいだ、がくせいは きいている, 'The whole time the teacher talks, the students listen' — きいている (listening) is itself durative, so it fills the entire span. The clause before あいだ stays in its plain/ている form; あいだ attaches directly, no に.

examples.ja: せんせいが はなしている あいだ、がくせいは きいている。
examples.en: The whole time the teacher talks, the students listen.

examples.ja: あめが ふっている あいだ、うちに いる。
examples.en: The whole time it's raining, (I) stay home.

examples.ja: やすみの あいだ、りょこうする。

antiPattern.ja: せんせいが はなしている あいだ、がくせいは ごはんを たべた。
antiPattern.why: たべた is a single completed POINT-event, not something that fills the whole span of the teacher's talking — that reading needs あいだに, not bare あいだ. あいだ alone is only for a second clause that is itself durative/continuous.

grammarPoints.rule: あいだに (間に) marks a single POINT somewhere inside a span, not the whole span — add に to あいだ when the second clause is a one-off completed event. せんせいが はなしている あいだに、がくせいは ごはんを たべた, 'At some point while the teacher was talking, the student ate' — the eating is one instant inside the talking-span, not something that filled it. This is the pairwise contrast partner of あいだ (aida-duration): same noun host, に is the whole signal.

examples.ja: せんせいが はなしている あいだに、がくせいは ごはんを たべた。
examples.en: At some point while the teacher was talking, the student ate.

examples.ja: あめが ふっている あいだに、がっこうへ いった。
examples.en: At some point while it was raining, (I) went to school.

examples.ja: やすみの あいだに、 ほんを かった。
examples.en: At some point during the vacation, (I) bought a book.

antiPattern.ja: せんせいが はなしている あいだに、がくせいは きいている。
antiPattern.why: きいている (listening) is durative — it fills the WHOLE talking-span, not one point inside it. That reading needs bare あいだ (aida-duration), not あいだに; swapping them here reverses which clause is supposed to be the single point.

grammarPoints.rule: うちに marks a closing WINDOW — do the second thing before the first state changes. あつい うちに、たべる, 'Eat while it's still hot (before it cools).' This is the same うち you know as 'home' (m16) — the sense widens from a physical space to a STATE's own space: 'within the state of X.' Contrast with あいだに (aida-ni-point): あいだに is a neutral point-in-a-span report; うちに adds urgency — the window is closing, so act now. Negate the first clause (ない うちに) for 'before X happens': かえらない うちに、でんわを する, 'before going home, make a call.'

examples.ja: あつい うちに、たべる。
いえに かえらない うちに、でんわを する。
examples.en: Before going home, (I) make a call.

examples.ja: コーヒーが つめたい うちに、のむ。
examples.en: Drink the coffee while it's cold.

antiPattern.ja: あつい あいだに、たべる。
antiPattern.why: あいだに just reports a neutral point inside a span — it doesn't warn that the window is closing. うちに carries that urgency (the food is COOLING); swapping in あいだに loses the 'before it's too late' feeling that's the whole point of choosing うちに here.

grammarPoints.rule: ところ (a moment) rides a verb's OWN tense to pin exactly where in an action you are — three tenses, three aspects, same host noun. Dictionary form + ところだ = about to start: たべる ところだ, 'I'm about to eat.' ~ている + ところだ = mid-action: たべている ところだ, 'I'm in the middle of eating.' た-form + ところだ = just finished: たべた ところだ, 'I just ate.' You already own all three verb tenses — ところ just asks which one, and reports where you are in the action.

examples.ja: いま たべる ところだ。
いま たべている ところだ。
examples.en: I'm in the middle of eating right now.

examples.ja: たべた ところだ。

antiPattern.why: This actually means 'I JUST ate' (た-form = just finished) — if you meant 'about to eat,' you need the plain dictionary form instead: たべる ところだ. The verb's own tense IS the whole signal; swapping it swaps the aspect completely.

grammarPoints.rule: ばかり after a noun says 'nothing but X, only X' — often with a complaining or exasperated tone about doing too much of one thing. ごはんばかり たべる, 'All (I) do is eat rice.' Different from the already-known だけ (a neutral 'just, only'): ばかり implies excess, like you're tired of it.

examples.ja: ごはんばかり たべる。
テレビばかり みる。
テレビばかり みた。
examples.en: All I did was watch TV.

antiPattern.ja: ごはんだけ たべる。
antiPattern.why: だけ is neutral — it just states the fact of eating only rice, no complaint. ばかり adds the 'too much of this, I'm tired of it' flavor; swapping in だけ drops that tone entirely.

grammarPoints.rule: ずつ after a counted quantity distributes it evenly across a group or across time — 'X each, X at a time.' ひとつずつ たべる, '(I) eat one at a time.' Unlike ばかり (which limits WHAT you do), ずつ describes HOW a quantity is spread out.

examples.ja: ひとつずつ たべる。
ふたつずつ かう。
ほんを ひとつずつ かった。
examples.en: (I) bought books one at a time.

antiPattern.ja: ひとつばかり たべる。
antiPattern.why: ばかり limits WHAT you're doing (nothing but eating), not how a quantity is spread. 'One at a time' needs ずつ; ひとつばかり would oddly claim you eat 'nothing but one,' not a distribution at all.

grammarPoints.rule: め after a counted quantity turns it into an ordinal — 'the Nth one.' ひとつめ, 'the first one'; ふたつめ, 'the second one.' This め is a DIFFERENT word from め 'eye' (m16) despite sharing kana — context always disambiguates, since this め only ever follows a counted number.

examples.ja: ひとつめは ごはんです。
ふたつめは テレビです。

antiPattern.ja: ひとつは ごはんです。
antiPattern.why: ひとつ alone just means 'one (item)' — it doesn't rank it in a sequence. Naming it as the FIRST in an ordered list needs the ordinal め: ひとつめ.

grammarPoints.rule: Drop ます from a verb's masu-form to get the masu-stem, then attach はじめる to mean 'start doing X' — the same attachment site as ながら/たい. たべはじめる, '(I) start eating.' This はじめる is the SAME verb from m33 ('to begin something'), now riding another verb instead of a plain noun object.

examples.ja: たべはじめる。
いま ごはんを たべはじめる。

antiPattern.why: The compound attaches to the BARE masu-stem (たべ), not the て-form — たべて はじめる isn't how this pattern works. It's たべはじめる, stem+はじめる fused directly, with no て in between.

grammarPoints.rule: Attach つづける to a masu-stem to mean 'keep doing X, continue doing X.' よみつづける, '(I) keep reading.' つづける (m30) has an intransitive partner つづく, 'to continue, to go on by itself' — つづける is something YOU do to a verb; つづく is something that just keeps happening on its own.

examples.ja: ほんを よみつづける。
ほんは まだ つづく。
しごとは まだ つづく。

antiPattern.ja: ほんは まだ つづける。
antiPattern.why: つづける needs a doer acting ON something — a book can't つづける itself. Something that 'just keeps going on its own' takes the intransitive つづく instead: ほんは まだ つづく。

grammarPoints.rule: たばかり and たところ both ride た-form + a noun host, but answer different questions. たばかり (ばかり on た-form) says 'just did X' — foregrounding how RECENTLY it happened, often with a note of surprise: かったばかりだ, 'I just bought it (barely any time has passed).' たところ (ところだ's た-tense, from L4) reports WHERE you are in the action's timeline — one of three possible tenses. Same underlying fact, different emphasis: ばかり foregrounds recency; ところ foregrounds sequence-position.

examples.ja: かったばかりだ。
たべた ところだ。
いったばかりだ。
しゅくだいを した ところだ。

antiPattern.why: This says 'I'm at the just-bought point' — grammatically fine, but if the emphasis is on how RECENT the purchase was (surprise: 'I only just bought this!'), かったばかりだ is the natural choice. ところだ tracks sequence-position; ばかり foregrounds recency.

grammarPoints.rule: まま after a plain-form (usually た-form) verb says a state is left exactly as it was — 'as is, unchanged.' かったまま だ, 'it's just as (I) bought it (untouched since).' まま is the STATIVE cousin of て-おく／て-ある: て-おく sets a state up on purpose for later use, て-ある reports a deliberately-arranged resulting state, but まま just names a state that hasn't changed — no deliberate setup implied, just 'nothing here has moved.'

examples.ja: ほんを かったまま だ。
examples.en: The book is just as (I) bought it (untouched since).

examples.ja: そのまま いる。
みたまま はなす。
examples.en: (I) tell it just as (I) saw it.

antiPattern.ja: ほんを かっている。
antiPattern.why: て-いる just reports an ongoing or resulting action (still in the state of having bought it) without flagging 'unchanged since.' まま specifically says nothing has been touched or altered — ほんを かったまま だ carries that 'still exactly as it was' flavor that ほんを かっている doesn't.

grammarPoints.rule: Attach おわる to a masu-stem to mean 'finish doing X' — the same attachment site as はじめる／つづける. たべおわる, '(I) finish eating.' Unlike L6's はじめる／つづける, this lesson budgets the past tense too: たべおわった, '(I) finished eating' — おわる (m32, already taught) is a live, ordinary verb with its own full conjugation, not restricted to dictionary form.

examples.ja: たべおわる。
たべおわった。
しごとは おわる。

antiPattern.why: The compound fuses directly onto the masu-STEM (たべ), not the dictionary form — たべる おわる isn't how the attachment works. It's たべおわる, stem+おわる fused with no space.

newAtoms.gloss: the space/time between — a span or interval
won't go back, doesn't go back — negative of かえる
only, nothing but — a quantity limiter
each, apiece — distributes a quantity evenly
the first one — ordinal of ひとつ ('one')
the second one — ordinal of ふたつ ('two')
to continue, to go on (by itself)
it's been a while, long time no see
as is, unchanged — leaving a state exactly as it was
just like that, exactly as it is

lessons.title: 「はなしている あいだ」「はなしている あいだに」— あいだ vs あいだに
lessons.focus: Core contrast: あいだ marks the whole span (second clause is durative), あいだに marks one point inside it (second clause is a completed event) — same noun host あいだ, に is the entire signal

lessons.title: 「あつい うちに」— うちに, contrasted against あいだに
lessons.focus: うちに: a closing window — act before the state changes. Same host word as うち ('home,' m16), sense widened to 'within a state.' Contrasted only against L1's あいだに (per spine), not against あいだ.

beats.ja: あつい うちに、たべる。
beats.en: Eat while it's still hot.

beats.ja: いえに かえらない うちに、でんわを する。

beats.ja: コーヒーが つめたい うちに、のむ。
beats.en: Drink the coffee while it's cold.

beats.ja: きゅうに あめが ふる。
beats.en: Suddenly it rains.
Eat while it's still hot.
beats.explanation: うちに warns that the hot-window is closing — eat now, before it cools. あいだに would just report a neutral point in a span, with no urgency; とき doesn't carry the 'before it changes' warning at all.

beats.audio: でんわを しない うちに、 しゅくだいを する。
beats.answer: Before making a call, (I) do homework.
distractors: While making a call, (I) do homework.

lessons.title: 「たべる ところだ」— ところだ, three tenses, one host
lessons.focus: ところだ rides the verb's own tense to report aspect: dictionary=about to, ている=mid-action, た=just finished. Cash-in ところ (fromModule future→m46, introducedByLessonId fixed off the dead ja-m9-1-2 pointer).

lessons.title: Review — ところだ／compound verbs, spiral back to あいだ／うちに
lessons.focus: Mid-third review: ところだ's three-tense card + たべはじめる／つづく mixed with a light spiral back to L1-L3's あいだ／あいだに／うちに — semantic clozes only (never bare が/を/は)

beats.ja: いま たべる ところだ。
beats.en: I'm just about to eat.

beats.ja: たべた ところだ。
beats.en: I just ate.
The work is difficult from the beginning.
beats.explanation: はじめ names a starting point. つづく describes something going on, and ところ (bare) names a place or moment, not specifically 'the beginning' — はじめ is the only fit.

beats.ja: たべはじめる。
beats.en: (I) start eating.

beats.ja: ほんは まだ つづく。
beats.en: The book still continues.

beats.audio: いま かえる ところだ。
beats.answer: I'm just about to go home.
distractors: I'm in the middle of going home.

beats.audio: しごとは まだ つづく。
distractors: The work is about to start.

lines.speaker: Mika
lines.ja: しごとは まだ つづく の？

lines.speaker: Ken
lines.ja: うん、いま しゅくだいを している ところだよ。
lines.en: Yeah, I'm in the middle of doing homework right now.

lines.speaker: Mika
lines.ja: わかった。

questions.q: What is Ken doing right now?

beats.ja: いえに かえらない うちに、でんわを する。
beats.en: Before going home, (I) make a call.

beats.ja: せんせいが はなしている あいだに、がくせいは ごはんを たべた。
beats.en: At some point while the teacher was talking, the student ate.

lessons.title: 「かったばかりだ」vs「たべた ところだ」— たばかり vs たところ, ひさしぶり
lessons.focus: Pairwise discrimination: たばかり (ばかり on た-form, foregrounds RECENCY) vs たところ (ところだ's た-tense from L4, foregrounds sequence-position). Vocab: ひさしぶり ('long time no see').

beats.ja: かったばかりだ。
beats.en: I just bought it.

beats.ja: いったばかりだ。
beats.en: I just went (there).

beats.ja: たべた ところだ。
beats.en: I just finished eating.
I just bought it (emphasizing how recent it was).
beats.explanation: ばかり foregrounds RECENCY — 'barely any time has passed.' ところ would shift the emphasis to sequence-position instead, and だけ drops the 'just now' sense entirely, leaving only a neutral 'bought only it.'

beats.audio: ひさしぶり！
ほんを かったばかりだよ。
distractors: I read a book a while ago.
I'm about to buy a book.

lines.speaker: Mika
lines.ja: ひさしぶり！げんき？
lines.en: Long time no see! How are you?

lines.speaker: Ken
lines.ja: うん、げんき。ほんを かったばかりだよ。
lines.en: Yeah, good. I just bought a book.

lines.speaker: Mika
lines.ja: そう。

beats.ja: かったばかりだから、あたらしい。
beats.en: Because (I) just bought it, it's new.

lessons.title: 「かったまま」「たべおわる」— まま stative, おわる compound (trio complete)
lessons.focus: まま (stative cousin of て-おく／て-ある, m30/m41) + 〜おわる compound (dict + one past, completing the はじめる/つづける/おわる trio). Vocab: そのまま, いっしゅん.

beats.ja: そのまま いる。
beats.en: (I) stay just as (I) am.

beats.ja: かったまま だ。
beats.en: It's just as (I) bought it (untouched since).

beats.ja: みたまま はなす。
beats.en: (I) tell it just as (I) saw it.

beats.ja: たべおわる。
beats.en: (I) finish eating.

beats.ja: たべおわった。
beats.en: (I) finished eating.

beats.ja: しごとは おわる。
beats.en: The work finishes.
The work finishes.
beats.explanation: おわる names the ENDING point. はじめ is a noun ('the beginning'), not a predicate here, and つづく would say the work keeps going — the opposite of finishing.

beats.audio: ごはんを たべおわったよ。
distractors: I'm in the middle of eating.

beats.audio: いっしゅんで たべおわった。
かったまま だ。
そのまま いる。

lines.speaker: Mika
lines.ja: ごはんは たべおわった？

lines.speaker: Ken
lines.ja: うん、いっしゅんで たべおわったよ。
lines.en: Yeah, I finished eating in an instant.

lines.speaker: Mika
lines.ja: いいね。

questions.q: How fast did Ken finish eating?

beats.ja: たべおわった ところだ けど、しごとは まだ つづく。
beats.en: (I'm) just at the point of having finished eating, but work still continues.

lessons.title: Review — full-module mixed: あいだ／うちに／ところだ／ばかり／compound verbs／まま
lessons.focus: Last-third review: every m46 grammar point + carrier vocab (うち/おわる/はじめる/つづける/だんだん) as already-known — semantic clozes only (never bare が/を/は)

beats.ja: せんせいが はなしている あいだ、がくせいは きいている。
beats.en: The whole time the teacher talks, the students listen.

beats.ja: いえに かえらない うちに、でんわを する。
beats.en: Before going home, (I) make a call.

beats.ja: たべた ところだ。
beats.en: I just finished eating.
All I did was watch TV.
beats.explanation: ばかり adds the 'nothing but this, tired of it' flavor. ずつ would distribute a quantity ('two at a time'), which doesn't fit a bare noun here, and だけ is neutral 'just' — it drops the complaining tone ばかり carries.

beats.ja: ひとつめは ごはんです。
beats.en: The first one is rice.

beats.ja: たべはじめる。
beats.en: (I) start eating.

beats.ja: ほんは まだ つづく。
beats.en: The book still continues.

beats.ja: かったばかりだ。
beats.en: I just bought it.

beats.ja: そのまま いる。
beats.en: (I) stay just as (I) am.

beats.ja: たべおわった。
beats.en: (I) finished eating.

beats.audio: ふたつずつ かった。
しごとは おわる。

lines.speaker: Mika
lines.ja: ひさしぶり！げんき？
lines.en: Long time no see! How are you?

lines.speaker: Ken
lines.ja: うん、げんき。ほんを かったばかりだよ。
lines.en: Yeah, good. I just bought a book.

lines.speaker: Mika
lines.ja: そう。

lessons.title: Challenge — timing & aspect, every frame in one arc
lessons.focus: あいだに, うちに, ところだ/ばかり contrast, compound verbs, まま — all combined with prior N4 grammar, no new vocabulary

beats.ja: がくせいが れんしゅうしている あいだに、せんせいは でんわを した。
beats.en: At some point while the student was practicing, the teacher made a call.

beats.ja: しゅくだいを しない うちに、テレビを みる。
beats.en: Before doing homework, (I) watch TV.
I just finished eating (emphasizing sequence-position, not recency).
beats.explanation: ところ foregrounds WHERE you are in the timeline — just past the finishing point. ばかり would instead foreground how RECENT it was, and とき just marks a bare 'when,' with no aspectual 'just' sense at all.

lines.speaker: Mika
lines.ja: ひさしぶり！げんき？
lines.en: Long time no see! How are you?

lines.speaker: Ken
lines.ja: うん、げんき。いま ごはんを たべはじめる ところだよ。
lines.en: Yeah, good. I'm just about to start eating rice now.

lines.speaker: Mika
lines.ja: そう。

questions.q: What is Ken about to do?

beats.ja: せんせいが はなしている あいだに、そのまま ごはんを たべおわった。
beats.en: While the teacher was talking, (I) finished eating just as (I) was, without a break.
